currentObjective: The dataset bug was the load-bearing one this session. Route handlers and pages were getting separate copies of the dataset because module scope in a production Next build is per route bundle, so an API write returned 201 and the public page never showed it — exactly what the codebase's own globalThis comment on leadStore warned about, but dataset itself was missed. After parking dataset on globalThis, an aggregate probe (rejecting 9 reviews on the demo vendor's products dropped the "approved reviews" KPI on /vendor/reviews from 36 to 28) proved route and page now share state. The vendor-reply guard was rewritten to post a unique marker and grep for THAT — the previous version asserted on "Your response", which also appears in the form label, so it stayed green on a false premise. The guard now genuinely proves the write reaches both /vendor/reviews and the product page. /vendor/reviews now also sorts Responded by respondedAt desc — the section heading promises most recent first and a slice of 10 was burying just-published replies.

what: getAdminMetrics().pendingProducts is now derived from getPendingProducts(50).filter(p => p.status === 'PENDING').length instead of the hardcoded literal 7.

It flows through three render sites: the KPI card on /admin (Pending listings), the 'Listing approvals' work-queue card on /admin, and the nav badge count on the admin sidebar (pendingReviews + pendingProducts). The PENDING StatusPills in the 'Product listings awaiting approval' table on /admin/moderation are the ground truth the count is derived against, so a moderator action (APPROVE / REJECT / FLAG) moves the KPI in lockstep with the table.

getAdminMetrics().pendingClaims remains the hardcoded literal 4, with a comment in the source flagging it as a deferred user decision: listing claims are P1.5 (not built). Deriving to 0 would empty the 'vendor claims open' hint and shrink the work-queue card to a single row; hiding the card is a visible product change; showing 0 under the label 'Pending listings' would be a label-is-a-claim violation per W7.
P2.3_pending_counters.why: Same W7 discipline as the verified-review labels: a KPI is a claim. The seeded catalogue carries 50 most-recently-updated products through getPendingProducts() and synthesises every third row as PENDING, so the queue length a moderator sees has always been a real number — only the KPI was lying. This was the cleanest P1-adjacent fix that did not require a deferred decision: it touches the data layer only, has no schema work, no UI work, and no PRNG order to preserve.

GUARD EXIT CODES are a three-way contract, not a boolean: 0 = every assertion passed, 1 = an assertion failed, 2 = the guard COULD NOT RUN (server not up, slug not derivable — first-load, lead-export, portal-runtime, review-submission and soft-404 all use 2 this way). Treating 2 as a failure is wrong (nothing is broken) and treating it as success is worse (nothing was checked). scripts/qa/run-all.mjs runs the whole suite in one command and keeps the three apart, retrying on 429 and labelling ENV separately from FAIL. It also flags any guard that exits 0 having reported zero checks, because a pass that verified nothing is not a pass. Prefer it over running guards by hand; it does not include the .sh browser guards, which need the split-run technique.
